uses.reason: This is the controlling supplied statutory text for the pleaded ground. The petitioner alleges exclusive possession and no written consent; respondent 1 denies any transfer or parting and respondents 2-4 describe employee accommodation and family visits. uses.incremental_value: Provides the statutory anchor against which the Delhi precedent and section 16 date/consent qualification can be read; other supplied corporate-transfer materials cannot replace these elements.
uses.limits: Current statutory reproduction; historical version is unverified. Only clause (b) is supplied and unrelated eviction grounds are outside scope.

uses.issue: Date and written-consent qualification for lawful subletting, including the pre-9 June 1952 statutory exception.
uses.reason: Section 16 can limit the clause (b) route if a qualifying subletting occurred before 9 June 1952 and the sub-tenant was in occupation at commencement of the Act; it also states that later subletting without written consent is not lawful. The record says M.L. Sharma was employed 'since 1952' and was provided accommodation, but it does not fix the accommodation date relative to 9 June or establish that the arrangement was a subletting.
uses.standalone_value: Supplies a potentially decisive historical-date exception and reinforces the written-consent rule; it cannot classify the employee accommodation or supply the missing exact date.
uses.incremental_value: Adds the main statutory qualification to section 14(1)(b)'s 9 June 1952 threshold, preventing an inference from the year '1952' alone.
uses.limits: Historical statutory version is unverified; application depends on facts absent from the supplied record, including exact start date and whether there was a sub-tenancy.

coverage_limits: The allowed case record ends at IK-110204406:L157 after respondent evidence closed; no supplied findings on the fixed ground or historical final outcome may be used.

The exact date when M.L. Sharma first received the accommodation is not fixed relative to 9 June 1952: the record says employment since 1952 and occupancy tied to employment, with other testimony only placing permitted use before 1972.

Written consent is disputed at the pleading level: the petitioner alleges no written consent and respondents 2-4 deny that the premises were given without written consent, but no operative written landlord-consent instrument is supplied.

The record refers to a 1 January 1973 notification by which New Zealand Insurance allegedly transferred to and vested in National Insurance, but the notification text and governing insurance-nationalization provisions are not supplied; bank, petroleum and company-amalgamation materials cannot fill that gap automatically.

The Delhi statutory reproductions supplied here state that their historical versions are unverified; the non-Delhi precedents and statutes retain their own stated jurisdictional, procedural and source limits.
